title: Globalization
hook: The world's economies have woven together so tightly that a decision in one country ripples through all the others — that deepening interdependence is globalization.
key_points: Globalization is the growing interconnection of economies, societies, and cultures across borders.
It is driven by trade, investment, migration, and especially communication technology.
It can raise growth and spread ideas, but also expose nations to shared shocks.
It challenges sovereignty: many problems and flows no longer stop at borders.
content_html: Globalization is the deepening interconnection of the world's economies, societies, and cultures — the process by which events and decisions in one part of the world increasingly affect people far away. It is not new in kind; trade routes and empires linked distant regions for millennia. What is new is the scale and speed. Goods are manufactured across supply chains spanning many countries, money moves around the globe in seconds, people migrate in large numbers, and ideas and culture spread almost instantly. The decisive accelerant has been technology: cheap transport and, above all, fast digital communication.
extra_html: Encyclopaedia Britannica describes globalization as encompassing economic, political, and cultural dimensions that are tightly intertwined. Its consequences are genuinely double-edged, which is why it is so politically contested. On one side, integration can raise economic growth, lift incomes, lower prices for consumers, spread technology and knowledge, and expose people to one another's cultures. On the other, it can expose national economies to shocks that originate elsewhere — a financial crisis or a pandemic in one region quickly becomes everyone's problem — and it produces winners and losers within each country, fueling backlash. For politics specifically, globalization poses a structural challenge to sovereignty: when goods, capital, people, pollution, information, and disease all cross borders freely, a single government acting alone struggles to manage them, which is part of why so much modern politics involves the difficult work of cooperation among states.

related.title: Trade & Protectionism
related.hook: Should a country trade freely with the world or shield its own industries? This single question has driven economic politics for centuries — and still does.

related.title: Global Inequality & Development
related.hook: Where you're born still shapes your life chances more than almost anything else. Closing that gap between rich and poor nations is one of politics' great unfinished projects.

related.title: Sovereignty Among Nations
related.hook: Inside its borders a state is supreme — but in the world of states there's no higher ruler. That gap, called anarchy, shapes everything about international politics.

flashcards.back_html: The growing interconnection of economies, societies, and cultures across borders, driven by trade, investment, migration, and technology.

flashcards.prompt: Which force has most accelerated modern globalization?

choices.text: Advances in communication and transport technology
The closing of all national borders

flashcards.explanation_html: Cheaper, faster communication and transport let goods, money, people, and ideas move across borders as never before.

flashcards.prompt: Why does globalization challenge state sovereignty?

choices.text: Many problems and flows no longer stop neatly at national borders

flashcards.explanation_html: When money, goods, people, pollution, and information cross borders freely, a single state struggles to control them alone.
